body.title: Declare analyzer.dataSourceListingTimeoutMs in the VS Code settings manifest
body.reproduction:
1. On main (a66eae5a), run the VS Code plugin suite: `cd vscode-plugin && npx tsx --test 'src/**/__tests__/*.test.ts'` (Node 22).
2. Two tests in vscode-plugin/src/config/__tests__/manifest-catalog.test.ts fail:
   - 'declared global insrc.* keys EXACTLY cover the global CONFIG_CATALOG paths (no missing, no extra)': manifest missing keys: insrc.analyzer.dataSourceListingTimeoutMs.
   - 'each declared key's type/enum/default matches its ConfigOption, and scope is 'machine'': no declared schema for insrc.analyzer.dataSourceListingTimeoutMs.
3. As a consequence (follows from the missing declaration; not yet checked in the editor): with the extension installed (0.5.14), VS Code Settings has no entry for the data-source listing timeout.

Expected: every global key in the daemon's config catalog has a matching insrc.* setting in the extension manifest, so the contract test passes and the setting can be edited from VS Code.
body.rootCause: The daemon's config catalog gained the global key analyzer.dataSourceListingTimeoutMs (src/config/config-catalog.ts:88: type number, default 120000), read by dataSourceListingTimeoutMs() in src/config/analyze.ts:479. It was introduced on 2026-10-10 by the work for ISSUE-008e146a. The VS Code extension declares its settings statically in vscode-plugin/package.json under contributes.configuration, and no insrc.analyzer.dataSourceListingTimeoutMs entry was added there. The manifest/catalog contract test (vscode-plugin/src/config/__tests__/manifest-catalog.test.ts), which imports CONFIG_CATALOG and compares it with the shipped package.json, catches exactly this drift. It was not run when the key was added.
body.fixIntent: Declare insrc.analyzer.dataSourceListingTimeoutMs in the extension's settings manifest so it matches the catalog entry (its type, default and description, with machine scope like the other global keys). The manifest/catalog contract test then passes and the setting is editable from VS Code. Check that no other catalog key has drifted the same way.
